narration.full_text: Namaste students! Today, we're diving deeper into solving linear equations using the algebraic method, specifically the elimination method. We'll also tackle how to solve complex word problems by translating them into mathematical models and then applying elimination. Our goal is to master the elimination method for solving linear equations, learn to solve complex word problems by setting up and solving equations using elimination, and finally, analyze real-world scenarios to translate them into mathematical models. Let's begin by looking at a system of two linear equations. We have 3x + 4y = 10 and 2x - 2y = 2. The first step in the elimination method is to clearly write down both equations. We will label them as Equation (1) and Equation (2) for easy reference. So, we have (1) 3x + 4y = 10 and (2) 2x - 2y = 2. This clear labeling helps us keep track of our work as we proceed with the elimination steps.
